text:
Edmonton has won five straight, outscoring teams 16-7, and almost nothing about the underlying play explains it. The Oilers took 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) in that stretch, and only 25% in Saturday's 5-2 win in Philadelphia. Over the whole season they sit at a plus-28 goal difference on chances that say they should be dead even. The gap is 22.9 goals of finishing above what their shots usually produce, plus 5.3 goals from the goaltending. Some of that is what happens when you employ Connor McDavid, whose point streak is now 22 games (12 goals, 41 assists), and Leon Draisaitl, at nine straight. Not all of it will last. Mike Babcock's first season behind the bench is off to a 35-point start either way, and our simulations give Edmonton a 98% playoff chance.

The most interesting Oiler might be in net. Devon Levi, given up on in Buffalo, has won his last five starts at 3.6 goals saved above expected and stops 91.3% of the hard shots. The Daily Faceoff and The Hockey News have both asked whether he is Edmonton's long-term answer. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, who took a puck to the face earlier this month, is off the out list and day-to-day.

Florida is still waiting on its captain. Aleksander Barkov (knee) has played two games this season and ESPN has him back around Nov. 27; Brad Marchand (knee) is targeted for Nov. 21. Lars Eller has filled in beside Sam Reinhart and Matthew Tkachuk, playing 16:38 a night. It has held up: the Panthers went 3-1-1 in their last five, including a 4-1 win in St. Louis on the night the Blues honored Hall of Famer Keith Tkachuk, with both of his sons on the scoresheet. Matthew Tkachuk reached 700 career points the next night in Dallas.

Our numbers have the Panthers slightly ahead tonight, 3.10 expected goals to 2.87. Watch special teams: Florida's power play creates 1.08 expected goals a game, the most of either side, and both teams spend plenty of time in the box.
headline: The Oilers keep winning games their chances say they shouldn't
